description: A dependency manager for .NET with support for NuGet packages and git repositories.
releaseNotes:
Paket 12 only ships as the `paket` .NET tool, which needs the .NET 10 runtime: `paket.exe`, `paket.bootstrapper.exe` and Mono are no longer supported. To upgrade, install Paket as a local tool (<https://fsprojects.github.io/Paket/installation.html#Moving-from-paket-exe-and-the-bootstrapper>). To keep `paket.exe` for now, remove the `version` line from paket.dependencies and run `.paket/paket.bootstrapper.exe --self`: you get the bootstrapper of Paket 11, which stays on the latest 11.x.

When the tool manifest declares paket, the restore during the builds and `#r "paket:"` in F# scripts run the local tool, before a Paket installed with `--tool-path`. Paket.Core targets net10.0 and drops its obsolete members, the command line no longer takes the syntax that Paket 5.5 replaced nor the `generate-include-scripts` and `fix-nuspec` commands, Paket no longer looks for projects in the folders whose name starts with a dot or that are links, and `paket pack --release-notes-file` reads the file with Fake.Core.ReleaseNotes 6.

This release also recognizes .NET 11, supports `.slnx` solutions, moves to the NuGet client libraries 7.9, writes paket.lock faster, and fixes many issues of git dependencies and of the restore. The next `paket install` or `paket update` may rewrite some framework restrictions of paket.lock, for the OS-specific frameworks of .NET 9 to 11 and in a shorter form.

* feat(BREAKING): Paket only ships as a .NET tool: `dotnet tool install paket`. `paket.exe` and `paket.bootstrapper.exe` are no longer built, and Paket no longer runs on Mono or the .NET Framework. See https://fsprojects.github.io/Paket/installation.html#Moving-from-paket-exe-and-the-bootstrapper
* feat(BREAKING): The release and `tools/paket.exe` of the Paket package carry a `paket.exe` stub instead, so that bootstrappers older than 11.0 explain how to move on: it prints the steps and exits with code 1. To stay on `paket.exe`, move to the bootstrapper of Paket 11, which stays on the latest 11.x: remove the `version` line from paket.dependencies, then run `paket.bootstrapper.exe --self`.
* feat(BREAKING): `Paket.Restore.targets` and `paket.targets` no longer run the bootstrapper or run `paket.exe` through mono. They find Paket installed with `--tool-path` (in `.paket` or the root), as a local tool, or on the `PATH` like a global tool. The `MonoPath` and `PaketBootStrapper*` properties are gone; the `PaketBootstrapping` target is kept, empty, for the projects that depend on it.
* fix(BREAKING): When the tool manifest declares paket, `Paket.Restore.targets` and `paket.targets` run the local tool instead of a Paket installed with `--tool-path` in `.paket` or the root, which can be an older Paket left by the move to the .NET tool, such as the `paket.exe` or bootstrapper of Paket 11. They skip it with the warning `PAKET0001`, on every OS, which `NoWarn` can turn off. To keep running it, set `PaketExePath` to its full path
* fix(BREAKING): When a `.config/dotnet-tools.json` or `dotnet-tools.json` up from the script declares paket, `#r "paket:"` in F# scripts runs that local tool instead of a Paket installed with `--tool-path` up from the script, which can be an older Paket such as the `paket.exe` or bootstrapper of Paket 11, and shows a warning. When the local tool isn't restored, it asks to run `dotnet tool restore` instead of running that Paket. As dotnet, it no longer looks for a manifest above an `isRoot` one
* feat(BREAKING): Paket.Core targets net10.0 instead of netstandard2.0 and net461: the projects and scripts that reference it must target net10.0 or later, as the `paket` .NET tool already needs the .NET 10 runtime. FSharp.DependencyManager.Paket stays on netstandard2.0 - https://github.com/fsprojects/Paket/issues/4317
* refactor(BREAKING): In Paket.Core, `Dependencies.DownloadLatestBootstrapper` and the `downloadBootstrapper` parameter of `Dependencies.Init` are removed, along with the `Releases` module, `Utils.isMonoRuntime`, `Utils.isMono`, `Utils.monoPath`, `Utils.fixArchive`, `ProcessHelper.monoArguments`, `ProcessHelper.appSettings`, `FrameworkDetection.resolveEnvironmentFramework` (replaced by `defaultScriptFramework`), `Queries.resolveEnvironmentFrameworkForScriptGeneration` and the `BootstrapperFileName`, `PaketFileName` and `GithubReleaseDownloadUrl` constants. `ProcessHelper.tryFindPath` and `findPath` take the `;`-separated paths instead of an app setting name. The `PAKET_PUSH_HTTPCLIENT` variable is gone: `paket push` always uses HttpClient.
* refactor(BREAKING): The obsolete `InstallModel.CreateFromLibs` and `InstallModel.createFromLibs`, `InstallModel.GetLibReferences` and `PlatformMatching.getFrameworkPathPenalty` of Paket.Core are removed: use `InstallModel.CreateFromContent` and `createFromContent`, `GetLegacyReferences` or `GetCompileReferences`, and `PlatformMatching.getPathPenalty`. So is the `Fake.Globbing` module that Paket.Core carried from FAKE 4: use `Fake.IO.Globbing.Glob` of the Fake.IO.FileSystem package. So are `NuGetCache.NuGetConfig.writeNuGetConfig` and `Constants.NuGetConfigFile`, unused since the end of the project.json support
* refactor(BREAKING): The obsolete `Dependencies.ShowOutdated` and `Dependencies.FindOutdated` overloads without the `force` parameter, `NuGet.GetLibFiles`, `NuGet.GetTargetsFiles`, `NuGet.GetAnalyzerFiles`, `InstallModel.GetReferenceFolders` and `FrameworkDetection.Extract` of Paket.Core are removed: use the overloads with `force` set to `true`, `NuGet.GetContent` with `NuGet.tryFindFolder`, `InstallModel.CompileLibFolders` and `PlatformMatching.extractPlatforms`, whose `Platforms` hold the framework. So is the `Dependencies.FixNuspecs` overload that takes the path of the `obj/*.references` file of a project: use the one that takes the `ProjectFile` and its `ReferencesFile`
* refactor(BREAKING): The obsolete `paket generate-include-scripts` and `paket fix-nuspec` commands, and the `references-file` option of `paket fix-nuspecs`, are removed: use `paket generate-load-scripts`, and `paket fix-nuspecs files <nuspec files> project-file <project file>` as `Paket.Restore.targets` does since Paket 5.92. The `.paket/Paket.Restore.targets` of an older Paket is replaced at the next `paket install` or full `paket restore`
* refactor(BREAKING): The paket command line no longer accepts the syntax that Paket 5.5 replaced, which it still took with a warning: the options without dashes, as in `paket add nuget Foo version 1.0`, `paket pack output bin buildconfig Debug templatefile paket.template` or `paket push file Foo.nupkg url https://example.org apikey KEY`, and the old names `--createnewbindingfiles`, `--creds-migrations` and `--references-files`. Write `paket add Foo --version 1.0`, `paket pack bin --build-config Debug --template paket.template`, `paket push Foo.nupkg --url https://example.org --api-key KEY`, `--create-new-binding-files`, `--migrate-credentials` and `--references-file` (once per file). The `.paket/paket.targets` of Paket 5.97.0 and earlier passes `--references-files`: the next `paket install` or full `paket restore` replaces it. The Ionide-Paket extension of Visual Studio Code, last updated in 2020, still passes this syntax to add, remove or update a package and to update a group
* fix(BREAKING): Paket no longer looks for projects and `paket.template` files in the folders whose name starts with a dot, like `.devenv`, nor in the folders that are links, as `paket convert-from-nuget` already did for the solutions and NuGet files: the projects there are left out of install, restore, update, remove and pack. Until now only `.git` and `.fable` were skipped. A cyclic link, as in a Nix `.devenv` profile, no longer makes the search run forever - https://github.com/fsprojects/Paket/pull/4421
* deps(BREAKING): `paket pack --release-notes-file` reads the file with Fake.Core.ReleaseNotes 6, in the formats described in https://fake.build/reference/fake-core-releasenotes.html: the package version is the first word of the latest header that is a whole SemVer version, so `## [1.2.3] - 2020-01-01` and `## v1.2.3 - 2020-01-01` give `2020-01-01`; pass `--version` for such headers. Prerelease versions like `1.2.3-beta.11.2` are no longer cut, and build metadata (`+sha.abc`) is kept - https://github.com/fsprojects/FAKE/pull/2686
* feat: The release carries the `paket.targets` and `paket.bootstrapper.exe` of the latest Paket 11 release, for Paket 11.0.0 and earlier, which download them from the latest release on `auto-restore on`, `convert-from-nuget` and `init`, and for the `--self` of the bootstrappers older than 11.0
* feat: `paket auto-restore on` writes `paket.targets` from Paket itself instead of downloading it from the latest GitHub release, so it works offline and matches the running Paket
* feat: `paket install`, `paket restore`, and `update`, `add` and `remove` when they install rewrite an existing `.paket/paket.targets` with the one of the running Paket, unless `PAKET_SKIP_RESTORE_TARGETS` is `true`, so that a repository that turned auto-restore on with Paket 11 no longer keeps the one that runs `paket.exe` through mono outside Windows and falls back to the bootstrapper. A restore with `--project`, `--references-file` or `--only-referenced`, like the one `paket.targets` runs during a build, leaves it as it is.
* feat: `#r "paket:"` in F# scripts finds the Paket .NET tool: installed with `--tool-path`, as a local tool of the manifest, as a global tool, or restored in the NuGet packages folder
* feat: Recognize the .NET 11 monikers: `net11.0`, `net11.0-windows...`, `net11.0-android` and the other OS-specific ones, and `netcoreapp11.0` - https://github.com/fsprojects/Paket/pull/4439
* feat: Add support for `.slnx` solution files - https://github.com/fsprojects/Paket/issues/4443
* feat: `paket convert-from-nuget` now updates `.slnx` solution files, as it does `.sln` ones - https://github.com/fsprojects/Paket/issues/4443
* perf: Faster framework restrictions: writing the lock files of large repositories takes a quarter of the time and allocates less than 40% of the memory it did - https://github.com/fsprojects/Paket/issues/4317
* deps: Update the NuGet client libraries from 5.11 to 7.9, along with System.Net.Http.WinHttpHandler and System.Security.Cryptography.ProtectedData
* deps: Update Argu from 6.1.1 to 6.2.5, and System.Configuration.ConfigurationManager from 4.7 to 10.0, so the `paket` tool no longer ships System.Drawing.Common 4.7 and its critical vulnerability (GHSA-rxg9-xrhp-64gj). The help of `paket update`, `paket find-packages` and `paket generate-nuspec` no longer shows their optional package ID, search text and `output` directory as required
* fix: The conditions written in project files now list the OS-specific frameworks of .NET 9 to 11 (`net9.0-android`, `net10.0-ios`, `net11.0-macos`...), which were left out in favour of their .NET 8 counterparts
* fix: The OS-specific frameworks of .NET 9 to 11 fall back to the previous .NET version for the same OS, as the Windows ones do: a `net11.0-android` project can use the `net10.0-android` assets and dependencies of a package
* fix: `paket install` no longer rewrites the framework restrictions of unchanged packages in paket.lock when it saves it for another reason, such as a removed `github` file, in groups with a `framework:` line: these restrictions are written in a single, shorter form, without empty clauses like `(&& (== net10.0) (== net461))`. The restrictions of the dependencies are rewritten once at the next `paket install`, and those of the packages when their group is resolved again; they hold the same frameworks
* fix: With MSBuild 15.8 or later, `paket.targets` skips the restore when `paket-files/paket.restore.cached` says that the last full restore, as by `paket install` or `paket restore` of all the groups and projects, was of the current `paket.lock`, instead of restoring on every build of a project without the SDK. It still restores while `paket.local` exists, when the `packages` folder is missing unless `paket.lock` has `storage: none` for all its groups, the main one included, and packages, and after it restored a project for another `paket.lock`, for a missing `packages` folder or with `paket.local`, until the next full restore
* fix: `paket restore` no longer skips as up to date when the `packages` folder is missing, or when a restore since the last full one may have changed it: a restore of some projects or groups for another `paket.lock`, one with `paket.local` or `--force`, or a full one for another `paket.lock` that failed. A full `paket restore --force` now writes `paket-files/paket.restore.cached`
* fix: `Paket.Restore.targets` and `paket.targets` read the closest `.config/dotnet-tools.json` and the closest `dotnet-tools.json` from the root up, instead of only the `.config/dotnet-tools.json` of the root, to know whether paket is a local tool, and only the paket tool counts, not another tool with a `paket` command
* fix: `Paket.Restore.targets` and `paket.targets` no longer take a folder named `paket` in the root or in `.paket`, such as a project folder named `Paket` on a case-insensitive file system, for a Paket installed with `--tool-path`
* fix: The restore no longer rewrites `.paket/Paket.Restore.targets` when only its line endings differ from the ones of Paket, as after a checkout with other line endings, which showed it as changed in git after each restore. The same goes for `.paket/paket.targets` and the other files that the restore writes
* fix: When the restore updates `.paket/Paket.Restore.targets`, as for a new version of Paket, the file keeps its line endings instead of taking the ones of the machine that built Paket. The same goes for `.paket/paket.targets` and the other files that the restore writes
* fix: When `#r "paket:"` in F# scripts runs the newest Paket .NET tool restored in the NuGet packages folder, as it does when it finds Paket neither installed with `--tool-path` nor as a local or global tool, it takes a release before its prereleases: with 12.0.0 and 12.0.0-alpha001 restored, it runs 12.0.0 instead of 12.0.0-alpha001
* fix: Git dependencies restore again when the git cache doesn't have their repository yet, as on a fresh CI agent: since 11.0.0, Paket ran `git remote set-url` in the empty cache folder that its lock had created - https://github.com/fsprojects/Paket/issues/4461
* fix: The paket-files of a git dependency are checked out when the HEAD of its git cache names a branch that is gone, as after the repository renamed its default branch, instead of failing with "bad revision 'HEAD'"
* fix: A git dependency whose checkout failed, as for a file name too long for the file system, is cloned again at the next restore, instead of being taken for one with local changes or for an up-to-date one
* fix: A local git dependency without a branch, whose repository has no master, gets an error that suggests giving its branch, as in `git file:///path/to/repository main`
* fix: A process that Paket starts and that exits right away, such as a git command, the `build:` command of a git dependency or a credential provider, no longer fails with "Start of process ... failed". For a local git repository, the error showed as "Could not find hash for ..."
* fix: Local git dependencies with a Windows path, like `git file:///C:/code/repo`, resolve again: since 11.0.0 and https://github.com/fsprojects/Paket/pull/4377, their path kept the `/` before the drive letter
* fix: A broken git cache in `~/.paket/git/db` is set up again instead of making git change the repository of a parent folder, such as a dotfiles repository in the home folder, and the git cache works with `safe.bareRepository=explicit`
* fix: The path of a local git repository can escape characters, like `git file:///home/me/my%20repo`, and its folder name is read from a Windows path that ends with `\` or doesn't exist yet, and from a path to the `.git` folder of the repository, like `git file:///home/me/repo/.git`. Such a path used to give an empty or a whole path as the name of the git cache and paket-files folders. A repository at the root of a file system, which has no folder name, or whose path ends with `.` or `..`, fails with an error. A folder name that holds a `%`, like `git file:///home/me/100%25`, is checked out too
* fix: A paket-files folder of a git dependency that isn't a clone, as one committed with the project, is cloned again. Paket used to run its git commands on the repository of the project instead, and could check the dependency out over the project
* fix: A git dependency on an annotated tag is locked at the commit of the tag, not at the tag object, which made each restore download it again. A lock file that holds the tag object still restores, and gets the commit at the next update
* fix: Only the `.git` that ends the name of a git repository, in any case as in `Repo.GIT`, is left out of its folder name, so `git https://github.com/me/me.github.io.git` goes to `paket-files/github.com/me/me.github.io` instead of `mehub.io`. The paket-files folder of a repository with `.git` inside its name, or another case of `.git` at its end, moves. A remote URL to the `.git` folder of a repository, like `git ssh://host/home/me/repo/.git`, is named after the folder of the repository, as a local one is, instead of taking the paket-files folder of its owner
* fix: The git cache of a repository is `~/.paket/git/db/<owner>/<project>`, so that remote repositories of the same name from two owners no longer share one, and swap its branches on each fetch. Local repositories of the same folder name still share one. Each repository is cloned again once, and `paket clear-cache` removes the old caches
* fix: `paket convert-from-nuget` removes the `NuGet.Config`, `NuGet.targets` and `NuGet.exe` files of the root `.nuget` folder again, as well as the folder once it is empty: Paket 11.0 had stopped finding them. It reads and removes the `NuGet.Config` of the root and of the `.nuget` folder under the names NuGet looks for, `nuget.config`, `NuGet.config` or `NuGet.Config`, and the `NuGet.targets` and `NuGet.exe` of the `.nuget` folder whatever the case of their name, where Linux only found lowercase names
* fix: `paket convert-from-nuget` converts and removes nothing through a link: it skips the projects, NuGet files and solutions of the folders that are links, with a warning for each such folder, so these projects are not converted. It leaves in place a `.nuget` folder that is a link and the solutions that are links, and skips with a warning the solutions it cannot read or update, instead of failing
* fix: `paket convert-from-nuget` only removes the solution items of a `.sln` that are files it deletes, found by their path in any solution folder. It removed the first line naming a NuGet file of `.nuget`, even a project or a `packages.config` it kept
* fix: `paket convert-from-nuget` keeps the non-ASCII characters of a `.sln` without a BOM, which it saved in ASCII
* fix: `paket generate-load-scripts` keeps in the group scripts the assemblies that reference themselves, like System.Reactive 7.0, which it dropped. It also keeps, with a warning, the assemblies and packages that depend on each other, which it dropped too - https://github.com/fsprojects/Paket/issues/4458
* fix: `paket update --no-install` no longer fails when a group has `generate_load_scripts: true` and the packages of the new paket.lock aren't all restored, as on a fresh checkout or for a package that the update adds: it leaves the load scripts to the next restore, which downloads the packages that they load - https://github.com/fsprojects/Paket/issues/2785
* fix: `paket pack --symbols` no longer fails on a project with Compile entries without an `Include` or `Update` attribute, such as `<Compile Remove="..." />` or a Compile item definition in an `ItemDefinitionGroup`, and leaves out of the symbols package the files that a Remove names without wildcards - https://github.com/fsprojects/Paket/issues/4222
* fix: Looking for projects no longer runs forever on a cyclic directory link, as in a Nix `.devenv` profile. `paket pack` still follows the links when it looks for template files - https://github.com/fsprojects/Paket/pull/4421 @michaelglass
* fix: Do not warn about missing "redirects: force" for FSharp.Core in projects targeting net5.0 and later - https://github.com/fsprojects/Paket/issues/4455
* fix: `paket install` no longer warns about missing "redirects: force" for FSharp.Core in SDK projects that take their target framework from Directory.Build.props, by inheriting it or through a property such as `$(DefaultTargetFramework)`. Paket, which doesn't read Directory.Build.props, also stops taking such a property for net10 (.NET Framework 1.0): where it needs the framework of the project, as for `framework: auto-detect` or `paket pack`, it falls back to net40, like for a project without framework - https://github.com/fsprojects/Paket/issues/4485
* fix: The warning about the FSharp.Core binding redirects of F# projects links to an existing section of the documentation
